title: Counit-normalized derived transport of coherent exact scalar comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to its module universe and let $R_0\to R_1\to R_2\to R_3$ be sheaves of commutative rings and $A_0\to A_1\to A_2\to A_3$ ordinary commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and their unbounded derived categories with localizations $Q_i$ for sheaves and $q_i$ for modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Put $T_{ij}C=C\otimes_{R_i}R_j$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and $t_{ij}N=N\otimes_{A_i}A_j$ termwise. Diagonal coefficient maps are identities. For all $i\le j$ assume these functors preserve every quasi-isomorphism. Let $G_i:\operatorname{Mod}(R_i)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_i)$ be additive functors whose termwise extensions preserve every quasi-isomorphism. Let $\theta_{ij}:t_{ij}G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_jT_{ij}$ be natural chain isomorphisms. Write $u_{ijk}$ and $a_{ijk}$ for the canonical balanced sheaf and module scalar associators $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes ab$, with inverse inserting $1$, and $m_i,\mu_i$ for the action units. Assume the following equations of natural chain maps:
$$G_k(u_{ijk})\theta_{jk,T_{ij}}t_{jk}(\theta_{ij})=\theta_{ik}a_{ijk},\qquad G_i(m_i)\theta_{ii}=\mu_i,$$
Assume also
$$u_{023}\,T_{23}(u_{012})=u_{013}\,u_{123,T_{01}},\qquad a_{023}\,t_{23}(a_{012})=a_{013}\,a_{123,t_{01}}.$$
Writing
$$r_C=\theta_{23,T_{12}T_{01}C}\circ t_{23}(\theta_{12,T_{01}C})\circ t_{23}t_{12}(\theta_{01,C}),$$
assume the iterated comparison equation
$$G_3\!\left(u_{023,C}\circ T_{23}(u_{012,C})\right)\circ r_C=\theta_{03,C}\circ a_{023,G_0C}\circ t_{23}(a_{012,G_0C}).$$
All these are equations of natural chain maps, with functor-composition constraints understood.

For sheaves let $\mathbb T_{ij}=-\otimes^L_{R_i}R_j$ be the specified K-flat derived change of rings, with its universal derived counit [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; let $\mathbb t_{ij}$ and $\mathbb G_i$ be the localizations of $t_{ij}$ and $G_i$, and $\mathbb a$ the localized module scalar associators. The localization $\overline T_{ij}$ of $T_{ij}$ has a unique natural comparison $c_{ij}:\mathbb T_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline T_{ij}$ whose component on each representative is the derived counit through the localization factorization. Transport through $c$ of the localized $u_{ijk}$ is the canonical ordinary derived scalar associator $\alpha_{ijk}:\mathbb T_{jk}\mathbb T_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb T_{ik}$. Every flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] has $T_{ij}P$ flat-term K-flat; the complexes $T_{jk}T_{ij}P$ and $T_{ik}P$ compute these two derived objects, and $\alpha_{ijk}$ and its inverse are represented by $u_{ijk,P}$ and its inverse under the counit comparisons.

There are unique natural isomorphisms $\Theta_{ij}:\mathbb t_{ij}\mathbb G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb G_j\mathbb T_{ij}$ whose representative components are the localized $\theta_{ij}$ conjugated by the specified localization and counit comparisons. They obey
$$\mathbb G_k(\alpha_{ijk})\Theta_{jk,\mathbb T_{ij}}\mathbb t_{jk}(\Theta_{ij})=\Theta_{ik}\mathbb a_{ijk},$$
the action-unit equation $\mathbb G_i(\mathbb m_i)\Theta_{ii}=\mu_i^D$, where $\mathbb m_i:\mathbb T_{ii}\to\mathrm{id}$ is the localized action transported through $c_{ii}$ and $\mu_i^D:\mathbb t_{ii}\to\mathrm{id}$ is the localized module action, and the four-stage associator and iterated-comparison equations obtained by replacing $T,t,G,u,a,\theta$ by $\mathbb T,\mathbb t,\mathbb G,\alpha,\mathbb a,\Theta$ in the assumed chain equations. On every flat-term K-flat resolution the maps are represented by the stipulated chain maps, and these maps and equations are independent of the resolutions. In particular all descended transformations are natural on every derived morphism: for any one of them $\tau:F\to H$ between the corresponding composite chain functors and any roof $C\xleftarrow{v}P\xrightarrow{f}J$ with $v$ a quasi-isomorphism, its localized version satisfies
$$\overline H(f)\overline H(v)^{-1}\overline\tau_C=\overline\tau_J\overline F(f)\overline F(v)^{-1},$$
where bars include the specified representative comparisons. No boundedness or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the stated preservation of every quasi-isomorphism to construct the three families of localized functors by Localization.lift, with Localization.fac. Form composite representative comparisons by whiskering and associating these factorization isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of whiskering by the localization descends chain natural isomorphisms by preimageIso.

proof.text: Apply changeOfRings_isKFlat_of_flat_terms_independentCoefficients to the supplied ordinary scalar functor and its object and morphism equations. Convert IsFlatOnSite to and from exactness of monoidal tensorRight by siteSheafTensorRightIso. This proves preservation of both K-flatness and flat terms. The computation clauses take a resolution as input, so no resolution-existence theorem is required.

proof.text: Descend u, a, m, mu, theta by conjugation with their composite representative comparisons. The preimageIso component equation and cancellation prove alpha_rep, a_rep, m_rep, mu_rep, theta_rep. Inverting the alpha square gives alpha_inv_rep. The theta square and full faithfulness prove theta_unique. The stipulated u and its inverse already specify the canonical scalar associator on representatives; no generic ringed-word descent theorem is used.

source.place: Tag 04VG; representative comparison and naturality calculus

proof.text: For triple coherence form the two natural transformations and use localization natural-transformation extensionality. Postcompose on a representative by G(sigma_ik) followed by gamma_k. Substitute alpha_rep and theta_rep, move comparisons using naturality of theta, gamma, delta and a, and combine images of compositions. The remaining equation is the assumed chain triple equation. Cancel the invertible postcomposition.

source.place: Tag 04VG; representative comparison and naturality calculus

proof.text: For the unit law use localization extensionality and postcompose by gamma. Substitute m_rep, theta_rep and mu_rep, and use naturality of gamma and the derived module unit. The remaining equation is the stipulated chain unit law.

source.place: Tag 04VG; representative comparison and naturality calculus

proof.text: For either four-stage associator law use localization extensionality and postcompose by the final representative comparison. Substitute the associator representative formulas. Naturality moves the internal comparisons past the inner associator. Both sides have the same leading comparison factors and the chain four-stage equality gives the result. This one categorical argument applies to both the sheaf and the module families.

source.place: Tag 04VG; representative comparison and naturality calculus

proof.text: The iterated comparison equation follows directly from triple coherence: use naturality of theta_23 at alpha_012 to move G(T_23(alpha_012)) left; combine the three t_23 images into the image of the triple equation for 012; substitute that equation; then apply triple coherence for 023. This proves the required iterated law without separately using the redundant assumed chain iterated equation.

source.place: Tag 04VG; representative comparison and naturality calculus

proof.text: For p:P to C a quasi-isomorphism, define the computation isomorphism as the inverse image of Q(p) under the derived functor followed by sigma_P. Its inverse is exactly the required expression, which determines it uniquely. For the two associator models use the same construction with the composite comparison and sigma_ik. Naturality of alpha on the inverse of Q(p), followed by alpha_rep, proves the forward formula; inversion gives the inverse formula. Finally roof_naturality follows from naturality on v and f after cancelling the invertible images of v and the representative comparison factors. No arbitrary resolution is chosen and no boundedness assumption is used.
